## 6. Static Content Deployment Strategies

### The Three Strategies

| Strategy | How It Works | Build Time | Disk Usage | Best For |
|----------|-------------|-----------|------------|----------|
| `quick` | Generates minimal set, symlinks rest | Fast | Low | **Cloud default** — large catalogs, many locales |
| `compact` | Symlinks shared files, copies unique | Medium | Low | Alternate Cloud option — watch for symlink breaks |
| `standard` | Full copy of all files for each locale | Slow | High | On-premise, debugging |

**`quick` is the default `SCD_STRATEGY` for Adobe Commerce Cloud.** `compact` is available but is not the default.

### Strategy Deep Dive

```bash
# quick strategy (Cloud default)
bin/magento setup:static-content:deploy --strategy=quick

# compact strategy
bin/magento setup:static-content:deploy --strategy=compact

# standard strategy
bin/magento setup:static-content:deploy --strategy=standard
```

#### quick (Cloud default)
```
pub/static/
  frontend/
    Magento/luma/
      en_US/          <-- minimal required files only
      _requirejs/     <-- symlinked/shared
      # Remaining files loaded on-demand or symlinked
```

#### compact
```
pub/static/
  frontend/
    Magento/luma/
      en_US/          <-- actual files
      fr_FR/          <-- symlinks to en_US where files are identical
                          copies where locale-specific
```

#### standard
```
pub/static/
  frontend/
    Magento/luma/
      en_US/          <-- full copy of ALL files
      fr_FR/          <-- full copy of ALL files (duplicated!)
```

**Exam focus:**
- `compact` uses **symlinks** — if the symlink target is missing (e.g., after cleanup), assets break. This is a common production issue
- `quick` is the default — faster because it **defers some file resolution** to runtime
- `standard` is the **safest but slowest** — never use in Cloud production
- The strategy is set in `.magento.env.yaml` under `SCD_STRATEGY`

### Configuration in .magento.env.yaml

```yaml
stage:
  build:
    SCD_STRATEGY: quick       # Default; use compact or standard as needed
    SCD_COMPRESSION_LEVEL: 4
    SCD_THREADS: 4
    SKIP_SCD: false
  deploy:
    SKIP_SCD: true   # Skip SCD in deploy if done in build
```

## 7. SCD Phase Placement — Architectural Decision

This is one of the most **exam-critical** architectural decisions in Cloud deployment.

### Option A: SCD in Deploy Phase (default behavior)

```
BUILD:  composer install, DI compile
            [fast build]
DEPLOY: maintenance ON --> SCD --> setup:upgrade --> maintenance OFF
            [long downtime = SCD time + upgrade time]
```

### Option B: SCD in Build Phase (recommended for production)

```
BUILD:  composer install, DI compile, SCD
            [longer build, but build = zero downtime]
DEPLOY: maintenance ON --> setup:upgrade --> maintenance OFF
            [short downtime = upgrade time only]
```

### The Tradeoff Matrix

| Factor | SCD in Build | SCD in Deploy |
|--------|-------------|---------------|
| Deploy downtime | **Shorter** | Longer |
| Build time | Longer | Shorter |
| Failed SCD impact | Build fails (not deploy) | Site stays down |
| DB required for SCD | No | No |
| Risk to production | Lower | Higher |
| Static assets from DB | Cannot use | Can use (but shouldn't) |

### How to Move SCD to Build

```yaml
# .magento.env.yaml
stage:
  global:
    SCD_ON_DEMAND: false
  build:
    SKIP_SCD: false          # Run SCD in build (default: false)
    SCD_STRATEGY: quick
  deploy:
    SKIP_SCD: true           # Skip SCD in deploy
```

**Exam focus:**
- The **architectural reason** to move SCD to build is **reducing maintenance window / downtime**, not build efficiency
- SCD in build **cannot access database** — if your theme/static content generation requires DB data, it must stay in deploy (but this is itself a design smell)
- Exam questions will present both options as "valid" — the correct answer is SCD in build **when minimizing downtime is the priority**
- `SCD_ON_DEMAND` generates static content on first request — useful for Staging/Integration, **not recommended for Production** (first-user penalty)

### Why SCD Doesn't Need the Database

```
SCD reads from:
  app/design/          (theme files — filesystem)
  vendor/              (module view files — filesystem)
  app/etc/config.php   (list of locales/themes — filesystem)

SCD does NOT read:
  Database             (no product data, no CMS content in static assets)
  Cache                (bypass cache during generation)
```

**This is why SCD CAN be safely moved to build phase.**

## 8. ECE-Tools Commands & Hooks

### ECE-Tools Command Structure

```bash
# Build phase commands
ece-tools build:generate   # Generates configuration, patches applied
ece-tools build:transfer   # Transfers generated files to mounts

# Deploy phase command
ece-tools deploy           # Runs full deploy sequence

# Post-deploy command
ece-tools post-deploy      # Runs post-deploy tasks

# Utility commands
ece-tools env:config:show  # Show current environment config
ece-tools config:dump      # Dump config to app/etc/config.php
ece-tools cron:enable      # Enable cron
ece-tools cron:disable     # Disable cron
ece-tools cron:kill        # Kill running cron jobs
```

### .magento.app.yaml Hook Configuration

```yaml
# .magento.app.yaml

hooks:
    build: |
        set -e
        composer --no-ansi --no-interaction install --no-progress --prefer-dist --optimize-autoloader
        php ./vendor/bin/ece-tools run scenario/build/generate.xml
        php ./vendor/bin/ece-tools run scenario/build/transfer.xml

    deploy: |
        php ./vendor/bin/ece-tools run scenario/deploy.xml

    post_deploy: |
        php ./vendor/bin/ece-tools run scenario/post-deploy.xml
```

**Exam focus:**
- The hook names are `build`, `deploy`, and `post_deploy` — note the **underscore** in `post_deploy`
- `set -e` in the build hook means **any failed command stops the entire build** — this is critical for fail-fast behavior
- Hooks run as the **application user**, not root
- You can add custom commands **before or after** the ece-tools calls — before for setup, after for custom post-processing
- The scenario XML files (`scenario/build/generate.xml`, etc.) are the extensibility points for custom steps

### Custom Hook Steps

```yaml
# Adding custom steps to build hook
hooks:
    build: |
        set -e
        # Custom pre-build step
        php artisan custom:pre-build-task

        # ECE-Tools standard build
        php ./vendor/bin/ece-tools run scenario/build/generate.xml
        php ./vendor/bin/ece-tools run scenario/build/transfer.xml

        # Custom post-build step
        bash scripts/custom-build-finalize.sh
```

### ECE-Tools Scenario Extensibility

```xml
<!-- Custom scenario extending build/deploy -->
<!-- app/etc/di.xml or custom scenario file -->
<scenario>
    <step name="custom-step" type="Vendor\Module\Step\CustomStep" priority="500"/>
</scenario>
```

**Exam focus:**
- ECE-Tools uses a **scenario-based architecture** — each phase (build, deploy, post-deploy) is a scenario composed of steps
- Steps implement `\Magento\MagentoCloud\Step\StepInterface`
- You can add/replace/remove steps by creating custom scenario XML files and referencing them in hooks

## 9. Zero-Downtime Deployment — Rolling Deploy on Pro

### Architecture

Cloud Pro uses a **rolling deploy** across its 3-node production cluster, not a true Blue/Green swap. The load balancer routes around each node as it deploys:

```
+------------------+        +------------------+        +------------------+
|   Node 1 (live)  |        |   Node 2 (live)  |        |   Node 3 (live)  |
|                  |        |                  |        |                  |
|  Serving traffic |-->Deploy|  Serving traffic |-->Deploy|  Serving traffic |-->Deploy
|  Current code    |        |  New code        |        |  New code        |
+------------------+        +------------------+        +------------------+
         |                           |                           |
         +----------+    +----------+    +----------+
                    |    |              |    |
                    v    v              v    v
              +------------+      +------------+
              | Load       |      | Load       |
              | Balancer   |      | Balancer   |
              +------------+      +------------+
                    |
                    v
               Users/CDN
```

### How Zero-Downtime Works on Cloud Pro

```
1. New code built into slug (artifact)
2. Deploy phase runs (setup:upgrade, cache flush)
3. Rolling deploy: LB routes around each node as it receives new code
4. After all 3 nodes updated: deployment complete
5. No single point of downtime — traffic always has at least one node serving
```

**Exam focus:**
- Zero-downtime rolling deploy is available on **Cloud Pro** — **not** on Cloud Starter
- "Zero downtime" is near-zero — brief windows exist during node transitions
- **Database migrations** (`setup:upgrade`) run once before the rolling deploy — if schema changes are applied while old code runs on other nodes, this requires backward-compatible migrations
- The shared database is the key constraint: during rolling deploy, old and new code may simultaneously read the same schema — schema changes must be backward compatible

### Backward-Compatible Migration Pattern

```php
// WRONG for zero-downtime rolling deploy — removes column while old code still reads it
class RemoveOldColumn implements SchemaPatchInterface
{
    public function apply(): void
    {
        $this->schemaSetup->getConnection()->dropColumn('sales_order', 'old_column');
        // Old-code nodes are still running and reading old_column = ERRORS
    }
}

// CORRECT — three-deploy pattern for rolling deploy with schema changes
// Deploy 1: Add new column, keep old column
// Deploy 2: Migrate data, switch code to use new column
// Deploy 3: Remove old column (all nodes now on new code)
```

## 10. Quality Patches Tool (QPT)

### What is QPT?

QPT (Quality Patches Tool) is Adobe's official mechanism for distributing isolated bug-fix patches without requiring a full version upgrade.

```bash
# Install QPT
composer require magento/quality-patches

# List all available patches and their status
bin/magento quality:patches:status

# Apply a specific patch
bin/magento quality:patches:apply MDVA-12345

# Revert a specific patch
bin/magento quality:patches:revert MDVA-12345

# Check if a patch is applicable to current version
bin/magento quality:patches:check
```

### QPT Status Output

```
+----------+--------+---------+------+------+------------------+
| Id       | Type   | Status  | Details                       |
+----------+--------+---------+------+------+------------------+
| MDVA-123 | Magento| Applied | v2.4.5 | Fix cart total bug  |
| ACSD-456 | Magento| N/A     | v2.4.6 | Not applicable      |
| MDVA-789 | Magento| Not applied | v2.4.5 | Fix search    |
+----------+--------+---------+------+------+------------------+
```

**Exam focus:**
- `quality:patches:status` shows **all** patches — applied, not applied, and not applicable
- QPT patches are **version-specific** — `N/A` means the patch doesn't apply to your current Magento version
- Patches are stored in `vendor/magento/quality-patches/patches/` directory
- QPT patches must be listed in `magento/quality-patches` package — you cannot create your own QPT patches (use `cweagans` for custom patches)
- On Cloud, QPT patches are applied during the **build phase** via the `quality:patches:apply` command in the build hook

### QPT in Cloud Context

```yaml
# .magento.app.yaml — applying QPT patches in build
hooks:
    build: |
        set -e
        composer install --no-ansi --no-interaction
        # QPT patches applied here, before DI compile
        php ./vendor/bin/ece-tools run scenario/build/generate.xml
        php ./vendor/bin/ece-tools run scenario/build/transfer.xml
```

```yaml
# .magento.env.yaml — specifying patches to apply
stage:
  global:
    QUALITY_PATCHES:
      - MDVA-12345
      - ACSD-67890
```

**Exam focus:**
- In Cloud, QPT patches are configured in `.magento.env.yaml` under `QUALITY_PATCHES` — **not** applied manually via CLI
- ECE-Tools reads the `QUALITY_PATCHES` list and applies them during the build scenario
- This is the **Cloud-correct** way — directly running CLI commands in hooks is possible but less maintainable

## 11. Custom Patches — cweagans/composer-patches

### What It Does

`cweagans/composer-patches` is a Composer plugin that applies patch files during `composer install` or `composer update`. Because `composer install` runs in the **build phase**, patches are applied at the earliest possible point — before DI compile.

### Setup

```bash
composer require cweagans/composer-patches
```

```json
// composer.json — patch definition
{
    "require": {
        "cweagans/composer-patches": "^1.7"
    },
    "extra": {
        "composer-exit-on-patch-failure": true,
        "patches": {
            "magento/module-catalog": {
                "Fix product save race condition": "patches/MDVA-99999-product-save-fix.patch",
                "Fix category tree performance": "patches/custom-category-tree.patch"
            },
            "magento/module-checkout": {
                "Custom checkout step fix": "patches/custom-checkout.patch"
            }
        }
    }
}
```

### Patch File Format

```diff
# patches/MDVA-99999-product-save-fix.patch
--- a/vendor/magento/module-catalog/Model/Product.php
+++ b/vendor/magento/module-catalog/Model/Product.php
@@ -245,7 +245,7 @@ class Product extends AbstractModel implements
      */
     public function save()
     {
-        $this->_beforeSave();
+        if ($this->getId()) { $this->_beforeSave(); }
         return parent::save();
     }
```

**Exam focus:**
- `"composer-exit-on-patch-failure": true` — **always set this in Cloud** — without it, a failed patch is silently ignored and broken code is deployed
- Patches are applied **alphabetically by package, then by description** — order matters for interdependent patches
- Patches apply against the **vendor directory** — after `composer install` unpacks packages
- If a patch fails (e.g., the upstream code changed), the entire build fails — this is the correct behavior
- Custom patches in `patches/` directory should be **committed to Git** — they're part of your codebase

### Patch File Location Best Practice

```
project-root/
  patches/
    MDVA-99999-description.patch     # QPT-style naming for tracking
    CUSTOM-001-checkout-fix.patch    # Custom prefix for internal patches
  composer.json                      # References patches/
  composer.lock                      # Locks exact versions
```

### Difference: QPT vs cweagans

| Aspect | QPT (quality-patches) | cweagans/composer-patches |
|--------|----------------------|--------------------------|
| Source | Adobe-managed catalog | Your own patch files |
| Applies | After composer install | During composer install |
| Config | `.magento.env.yaml` | `composer.json` |
| Rollback | `quality:patches:revert` | Remove from composer.json |
| Use case | Official Adobe bug fixes | Custom/third-party fixes |
| Auditable | Yes (patch ID tracking) | Manual tracking |

## 12. Security Patches — Full vs Isolated

### Full Security Patches

A full security patch (e.g., `2.4.5` → `2.4.5-p1`) is a **complete release** that:
- Includes all security fixes
- May include additional bug fixes
- Requires full `composer update magento/product-community-edition`
- Tested against the full dependency tree

```bash
# Applying a full security patch on Cloud
# Update composer.json first:
composer require magento/product-cloud-edition:2.4.6-p1 --no-update
composer update
git add composer.json composer.lock
git commit -m "Security patch 2.4.6-p1"
git push
```

### Isolated Security Patches (APSB Patches)

Isolated patches address a **specific CVE** without a full version bump:
- Smaller scope — only the vulnerable files
- Faster to apply and test
- Distributed as patch files (`.patch`) or via QPT
- Lower risk of regression

```bash
# Applying an isolated security patch via QPT
bin/magento quality:patches:apply APSB23-99

# Or via cweagans if distributed as a patch file
# Add to composer.json patches section
```

### PCI SLA Requirements

```
Critical Security Patches (CVSS >= 9.0):
  Apply within: 30 days of release
  (some PCI DSS interpretations: 72 hours for critical)

High Security Patches (CVSS 7.0-8.9):
  Apply within: 30 days

Medium/Low:
  Apply within: 90 days
```

**Exam focus:**
- **Full patches** = new Magento version (e.g., -p1, -p2) — preferred when available
- **Isolated patches** = targeted fix for a specific CVE without version bump — used when full patch not yet available or cannot be applied immediately
- PCI DSS requires patching **within defined SLAs** — failing to patch within SLA is a compliance violation
- On Cloud, applying a full security patch = `composer update` + redeploy through the pipeline
- Never apply patches directly to Cloud production files — always go through Git pipeline

## 13. Dependency Management in Cloud

### The Core Constraint

> **On Adobe Commerce Cloud, you cannot run arbitrary `composer update` — you must use the Adobe-managed dependency set.**

```
On-Premise Mental Model:        Cloud Mental Model:
  You control versions             Adobe controls baseline
  composer update = fine           composer update = risky
  Any package version              Must align with Cloud modules
```

### Why Arbitrary composer update Is Dangerous on Cloud

```
ECE-Tools depends on specific versions of:
  - symfony/console
  - illuminate/container
  - guzzlehttp/guzzle
  - etc.

Your modules may require:
  - symfony/console ^5.0

ECE-Tools requires:
  - symfony/console ^4.4

Result: Dependency conflict that breaks ECE-Tools
        = Deployment infrastructure broken
        = Cannot deploy to Cloud
```

### Safe Dependency Update Pattern on Cloud

```bash
# WRONG — blind update
composer update

# CORRECT — targeted update of specific package
composer update vendor/package --with-dependencies

# CORRECT — check for conflicts before committing
composer update vendor/package --dry-run

# CORRECT — use Cloud-compatible metapackage update
composer require magento/magento-cloud-metapackage:^2.4.6 --no-update
composer update
```

### The magento-cloud-metapackage

```json
// composer.json — Cloud projects must use this metapackage
{
    "require": {
        "magento/magento-cloud-metapackage": ">=2.4.6 <2.4.7",
        "magento/ece-tools": "^2002.1.0"
    }
}
```

**Exam focus:**
- `magento/magento-cloud-metapackage` pins the versions of all Cloud-specific dependencies — updating outside this set can break `ece-tools`
- The correct approach for adding new packages: `composer require vendor/package` (adds to `composer.json`) then push — **do not** run broad `composer update`
- Composer's **conflict resolution** during `composer install` (using `composer.lock`) is safe — it's `composer update` (modifying `composer.lock`) that is dangerous
- In Cloud, `composer.lock` should **always be committed** — it pins exact versions used in build

### Dependency Conflict Scenario (Exam-style)

```
SCENARIO: A developer needs to add a new third-party module that requires
symfony/http-kernel ^6.0, but the current Cloud environment uses ^5.4.

WRONG answer: "Run composer update to resolve conflicts"
CORRECT answer: "Check if the module has a compatible version that supports
                 symfony/http-kernel ^5.4, or request an exception with
                 Adobe Commerce support, or defer until Cloud's baseline
                 upgrades to symfony ^6.0"
```

## 14. Scenario-Based Architectural Reasoning

These are the types of reasoning chains the exam tests.

### Scenario 1: "The deployment takes 15 minutes. How do you reduce downtime?"

```
Analysis:
  - 15 min deploy = probably SCD in deploy phase
  - SCD for large catalog with many locales = 10-12 min alone

Wrong answers:
  A) "Use faster servers"           -- not architectural
  B) "Reduce number of locales"     -- may not be acceptable
  C) "Use quick strategy"           -- helps but doesn't solve root cause

Correct answer:
  D) "Move SCD to build phase"
     Reasoning: SCD doesn't require DB, can run in build,
                eliminates SCD time from maintenance window,
                build time increases but build = no downtime
```

### Scenario 2: "A custom module works locally but fails in Cloud build"

```
Analysis:
  - "Fails in Cloud build" + "works locally" = build environment difference
  - Build has NO database
  - Local dev has database always available

Wrong answers:
  A) "Increase build timeout"               -- not the root cause
  B) "Add the module to the build phase"    -- nonsensical
  C) "Clear generated code and retry"       -- won't fix root cause

Correct answer:
  D) "The module connects to DB in constructor or during DI compile"
     Reasoning: Build phase has no DB connection. Fix = lazy-load
                the DB dependency (proxy pattern or deferred access)
```

### Scenario 3: "Which patch mechanism for an urgent CVE fix?"

```
SITUATION: Critical CVE discovered. Full patch (2.4.6-p2) not yet released.
           CVE has isolated patch file from Adobe Security.

Analysis:
  - Full patch not available
  - Isolated patch available
  - PCI SLA requires action within 30 days (or 72 hours for critical)

Correct answer:
  Apply isolated patch via cweagans or QPT immediately
  Plan full patch upgrade when available
  Document in security log for PCI audit trail

Key reasoning: Isolated patch = smaller blast radius, faster to test,
               meets PCI SLA. Waiting for full patch = PCI violation.
```

### Scenario 4: "Developer wants to run composer update to add a module"

```
SITUATION: New third-party module needed in Cloud production.
           Developer proposes: "composer update && git push"

Analysis:
  - composer update resolves ALL dependencies, not just new package
  - May upgrade ECE-Tools dependencies
  - May break ece-tools functionality
  - Cloud-managed dependency set disrupted

Correct answer:
  composer require vendor/new-module
  composer update vendor/new-module --with-dependencies
  Review composer.lock diff carefully
  Test in Integration environment first

Do NOT: composer update (broad)
```

### Scenario 5: "Post-deploy reindex vs deploy-phase reindex"

```
QUESTION: When should reindex happen during deployment?

Deploy-phase reindex:
  PRO: Data consistent before site goes live
  CON: Adds to maintenance window (downtime)
  CON: Large catalog = very long downtime

Post-deploy reindex:
  PRO: Site available immediately after deploy
  CON: Brief period of stale search/catalog data
  CON: Reindex runs while site serves traffic (resource contention)

Correct architectural answer:
  For most scenarios: Post-deploy (minimize downtime)
  Exception: If stale data is unacceptable (e.g., pricing reindex
             after price update deployment) = deploy phase
  Best practice: Avoid index-impacting deployments during peak hours
```

---

## Quick-Reference Checklist

### Three Deployment Phases

- [ ] **Build phase**: No DB, no services — composer install, DI compile, SCD (optional), generates immutable artifact
- [ ] **Deploy phase**: DB available, maintenance ON — setup:upgrade, cache flush, maintenance OFF
- [ ] **Post-deploy phase**: Site live — warmup, cron start, optional reindex
- [ ] Hook names in `.magento.app.yaml`: `build`, `deploy`, `post_deploy` (underscore!)

### Build Phase Critical Facts

- [ ] No database connection in build phase — ever
- [ ] Code connecting to DB in constructor fails in build (silent or fatal)
- [ ] Writable mounts (`var/`, `pub/media/`) not available during build
- [ ] `env.php` does not contain DB credentials during build
- [ ] DI compile happens in build — interceptors/proxies generated here

### Patch Interfaces (setup:upgrade)

- [ ] `DataPatchInterface` — for data patches (DML/DQL: row inserts, data migrations)
- [ ] `SchemaPatchInterface` — for schema patches (DDL: table/column changes)
- [ ] Both extend `PatchInterface`, which declares `apply()` and `getAliases()`
- [ ] `PatchInterface` extends `DependentPatchInterface`, which declares `getDependencies()` (static)
- [ ] `getDependencies()` ensures patch ordering; `getAliases()` prevents re-applying renamed patches
- [ ] Idempotence enforced by `patch_list` DB table — each patch applied exactly once

### SCD Strategies

- [ ] `quick` = **Cloud default** — minimal generation, symlinks rest — fastest build
- [ ] `compact` = symlinks shared, copies unique — alternate Cloud option — **watch for broken symlinks**
- [ ] `standard` = full copy per locale — slowest, most disk — on-premise only
- [ ] Moving SCD to build = shorter maintenance window (architecturally preferred for production)
- [ ] `SCD_ON_DEMAND` = runtime generation — Staging/Integration only, not Production
- [ ] SCD does NOT require database — safe to run in build phase

### ECE-Tools Commands

- [ ] `ece-tools build:generate` — generates config files
- [ ] `ece-tools build:transfer` — moves artifacts to mounts
- [ ] `ece-tools deploy` — full deploy sequence
- [ ] `ece-tools post-deploy` — post-deploy tasks
- [ ] Scenario files: `scenario/build/generate.xml`, `scenario/deploy.xml`, `scenario/post-deploy.xml`

### Quality Patches Tool (QPT)

- [ ] `bin/magento quality:patches:status` — list all patch statuses
- [ ] `bin/magento quality:patches:apply MDVA-XXXXX` — apply a patch
- [ ] `bin/magento quality:patches:revert MDVA-XXXXX` — revert a patch
- [ ] Cloud: configure via `QUALITY_PATCHES` in `.magento.env.yaml`
- [ ] Cannot create your own QPT patches — use `cweagans` for custom patches

### Custom Patches (cweagans)

- [ ] `cweagans/composer-patches` applies patches during `composer install`
- [ ] Always set `"composer-exit-on-patch-failure": true`
- [ ] Patch files committed to Git in `patches/` directory
- [ ] Applies **during build phase** — earliest possible application point
- [ ] Failed patch = build fails = correct behavior (not silent)

### Security Patches

- [ ] **Full patch** = new Magento version (e.g., -p1) — complete security release
- [ ] **Isolated patch** = specific CVE fix — smaller scope, faster to apply
- [ ] PCI SLA: Critical = 30 days (some interpretations: 72 hours); High = 30 days
- [ ] Apply isolated patch immediately if full patch not available — meets PCI SLA
- [ ] Always deploy through Git pipeline — never patch files directly

### Dependency Management in Cloud

- [ ] Never run arbitrary `composer update` on Cloud
- [ ] Use `composer require vendor/package` for new packages
- [ ] Use `magento/magento-cloud-metapackage` to pin Cloud-compatible versions
- [ ] Always commit `composer.lock` — pins exact build versions
- [ ] Breaking Cloud dependencies = broken deployment infrastructure

### Zero-Downtime (Rolling Deploy on Pro)

- [ ] Rolling deploy across **3-node cluster** — available on **Cloud Pro only** — not Starter
- [ ] Each node updated sequentially; LB routes around deploying node
- [ ] DB migrations (`setup:upgrade`) run once before rolling deploy starts
- [ ] Old and new code may run simultaneously on different nodes → schema changes must be backward compatible
- [ ] Three-deploy pattern for breaking schema changes (add → migrate → drop)
- [ ] "Zero downtime" is near-zero — brief node transition windows exist

### Architectural Decision Framework (Exam)

- [ ] **SCD in build** = preferred for production, reduces downtime
- [ ] **Reindex in post-deploy** = preferred, unless data consistency is critical
- [ ] **Lazy DB access** = required pattern for Cloud-compatible code
- [ ] **Isolated patch first** = when full patch unavailable and PCI SLA active
- [ ] **Targeted composer update** = only update specific package + its deps
- [ ] **Test in Integration → Staging → Production** = required pipeline discipline

---

*Study notes generated for Adobe Commerce Architect Certification — Week 3, Section 2 & 3*
*Focus: Deployment decisions are architectural — always reason from WHY, not just WHAT*

flashcards.question: What is the consequence of a custom module calling the database inside a constructor on Adobe Commerce Cloud?
flashcards.answer: The build phase has no database connection, so a constructor-level DB call causes a fatal error or silent failure during DI compilation, breaking the build. The fix is lazy/deferred DB access.
flashcards.hint: Consider what services are unavailable in the isolated build container.
flashcards.topic: Apr 29 — Deployment Pipeline, ECE-Tools & Quality Patches

flashcards.question: What does getDependencies() do in the patch system, and which interface declares it?
flashcards.answer: getDependencies() is a static method declared by DependentPatchInterface (which PatchInterface extends). It returns an array of patch class names that must be applied before the current patch, ensuring correct application order.
flashcards.hint: This is the method that controls patch ordering — not the one that handles renames.
flashcards.topic: Apr 29 — Deployment Pipeline, ECE-Tools & Quality Patches

flashcards.question: What is the default SCD strategy on Adobe Commerce Cloud, and why is the 'compact' strategy risky in production?
flashcards.answer: The default SCD strategy is 'quick', which generates a minimal file set and defers the rest. The 'compact' strategy uses symlinks for shared files — if the symlink target is missing after cleanup, assets break in production.
flashcards.hint: The riskiest strategy for production is the one that relies on filesystem references rather than copies.
flashcards.topic: Apr 29 — Deployment Pipeline, ECE-Tools & Quality Patches

flashcards.question: Why is SCD_ON_DEMAND not recommended for Cloud production environments?
flashcards.answer: SCD_ON_DEMAND generates static content on the first request, imposing a first-user performance penalty. It is appropriate for Staging and Integration environments but not for Production.
flashcards.hint: Think about who pays the cost of generation when it's deferred to request time.
flashcards.topic: Apr 29 — Deployment Pipeline, ECE-Tools & Quality Patches

flashcards.question: What is the purpose of setting 'composer-exit-on-patch-failure': true in composer.json when using cweagans/composer-patches?
flashcards.answer: Without this setting, a patch failure is silently ignored and broken or unpatched code is deployed. Setting it to true ensures a failed patch stops the build immediately, preventing silent defects.
flashcards.hint: The default behavior of cweagans on patch failure is the dangerous behavior you're overriding.
flashcards.topic: Apr 29 — Deployment Pipeline, ECE-Tools & Quality Patches

flashcards.question: What is the key difference between QPT (Quality Patches Tool) and cweagans/composer-patches regarding who can create patches and how they are configured on Cloud?
flashcards.answer: QPT patches are Adobe-managed and configured via QUALITY_PATCHES in .magento.env.yaml; you cannot create your own QPT patches. cweagans applies your own custom or third-party patch files configured in composer.json.
flashcards.hint: One is Adobe's catalog, one is your own patch files — they also differ in where Cloud configuration lives.
flashcards.topic: Apr 29 — Deployment Pipeline, ECE-Tools & Quality Patches

flashcards.question: In a Cloud rolling deploy on Pro, why must database schema changes be backward compatible, and what is the three-deploy pattern?
flashcards.answer: During a rolling deploy, old and new code run simultaneously on different nodes against the same database. To avoid errors, schema changes must be backward compatible. The three-deploy pattern is: Deploy 1 adds the new column, Deploy 2 migrates data and switches code, Deploy 3 removes the old column.
flashcards.hint: Consider what happens when Node 1 has new code but Nodes 2 and 3 still run old code against the updated schema.
flashcards.topic: Apr 29 — Deployment Pipeline, ECE-Tools & Quality Patches

flashcards.question: Zero-downtime rolling deployment is available on which Adobe Commerce Cloud tier, and what is the key infrastructure enabling it?
flashcards.answer: Rolling deployment is available on Cloud Pro only (not Cloud Starter). It works via a 3-node production cluster where the load balancer routes traffic around each node as it receives and activates the new code.
flashcards.hint: The tier distinction is a common exam trap — one tier gets near-zero downtime, the other does not.
flashcards.topic: Apr 29 — Deployment Pipeline, ECE-Tools & Quality Patches

flashcards.question: What is the correct Cloud approach when a developer needs to add a new third-party Composer package, and what command is dangerous to run?
flashcards.answer: Use 'composer require vendor/package' to add only the new package, then 'composer update vendor/package --with-dependencies' to resolve its deps. Running broad 'composer update' is dangerous because it may upgrade ECE-Tools dependencies and break the deployment infrastructure.
flashcards.hint: The dangerous command updates everything in composer.lock, not just the new package.
flashcards.topic: Apr 29 — Deployment Pipeline, ECE-Tools & Quality Patches

flashcards.question: What is the correct action when a critical CVE isolated patch is available but the corresponding full security patch (e.g., -p1) has not yet been released?
flashcards.answer: Apply the isolated patch immediately via cweagans or QPT to meet PCI DSS SLA requirements. Plan the full patch upgrade when available. Waiting for the full patch risks a PCI compliance violation.
flashcards.hint: PCI SLA compliance drives the urgency — what is the smallest-scope fix you can apply right now?
flashcards.topic: Apr 29 — Deployment Pipeline, ECE-Tools & Quality Patches

flashcards.question: What is the hook name for the post-deploy phase in .magento.app.yaml, and what is a critical behavioral difference between post-deploy failures and deploy failures?
flashcards.answer: The hook name is post_deploy (underscore, not hyphen). A failure in post-deploy does not take the site down because the site is already live when post-deploy runs, unlike a deploy-phase failure which can leave maintenance mode ON.
flashcards.hint: The naming is a syntax trap. The behavioral difference relates to site availability when each phase executes.
flashcards.topic: Apr 29 — Deployment Pipeline, ECE-Tools & Quality Patches

flashcards.question: Why does moving SCD to the build phase reduce deployment downtime, and what architectural constraint makes this safe?
flashcards.answer: SCD does not require database access — it reads only from filesystem sources (theme files, vendor, config.php). Moving it to build eliminates SCD time from the maintenance window, since build phase has zero downtime.
flashcards.hint: Think about what SCD actually reads from, and which phase is the only one with actual site downtime.
flashcards.topic: Apr 29 — Deployment Pipeline, ECE-Tools & Quality Patches

flashcards.question: Which writable mounts are unavailable during the Cloud build phase, and why does this matter?
flashcards.answer: Mounts such as var/ and pub/media/ are not available during build. Any code or process that writes to these paths during build will fail, and env.php does not contain DB credentials at build time.
flashcards.hint: The build produces an immutable artifact — think about what 'read-only filesystem' implies for runtime mounts.
flashcards.topic: Apr 29 — Deployment Pipeline, ECE-Tools & Quality Patches

flashcards.question: What is the difference between DataPatchInterface and SchemaPatchInterface, and what shared method enforces idempotence?
flashcards.answer: DataPatchInterface handles DML/DQL operations (row inserts, data migrations); SchemaPatchInterface handles DDL operations (table/column changes). Both extend PatchInterface which declares apply() and getAliases(). Idempotence is enforced by the patch_list DB table — each patch runs exactly once.
flashcards.hint: One handles rows, one handles structure. Think about what prevents a patch from running twice after a rename.
flashcards.topic: Apr 29 — Deployment Pipeline, ECE-Tools & Quality Patches

flashcards.question: What are the two ECE-Tools sub-commands that compose the build hook, and what does each one do?
flashcards.answer: ece-tools build:generate creates configuration files from environment variables, and ece-tools build:transfer moves the generated artifacts to the application's mount points. Both are invoked via their scenario XML files in the hooks configuration.
flashcards.hint: One creates config, one moves artifacts — think generate then transfer.
flashcards.topic: Apr 29 — Deployment Pipeline, ECE-Tools & Quality Patches

studyNotes.title: Day 19 — Configuration Management + Troubleshooting
studyNotes.content:
# Magento 2 Configuration Management & Troubleshooting
## Adobe Certified Professional – Architect Exam Study Notes

---

## Table of Contents

1. [Configuration File Architecture](#1-configuration-file-architecture)
2. [The Configuration Hierarchy](#2-the-configuration-hierarchy)
3. [app:config:dump — Deep Dive](#3-appconfig-dump--deep-dive)
4. [Environment Variables as Configuration Overrides](#4-environment-variables-as-configuration-overrides)
5. [Application Modes](#5-application-modes)
6. [Log Files — What Each Contains](#6-log-files--what-each-contains)
7. [Common Failure Patterns & Diagnosis](#7-common-failure-patterns--diagnosis)
8. [The Correct Upgrade / Deploy Order](#8-the-correct-upgrade--deploy-order)
9. [Hands-On: Breaking & Diagnosing a Plugin](#9-hands-on-breaking--diagnosing-a-plugin)
10. [Architect-Level Decision Frameworks](#10-architect-level-decision-frameworks)
11. [Quick-Reference Checklist](#quick-reference-checklist)

---

## 1. Configuration File Architecture

Magento 2 splits its configuration across multiple files and storage layers. Understanding *why* each file exists is more important on the architect exam than memorising syntax.

### 1.1 The Two Critical PHP Config Files

```
app/
  etc/
    config.php        <-- COMMITTED to VCS
    env.php           <-- NEVER committed to VCS
```

| File | Purpose | Committed? | Editable via Admin UI? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `config.php` | Shared system config, module enable/disable list, store config snapshot | **Yes** | No — locked after dump |
| `env.php` | Environment-specific: DB, cache, session, crypt key | **No** | No — CLI or direct file edit only |

### 1.2 config.php — Structure

Generated by `bin/magento app:config:dump`. Contains:

```php
<?php
return [
    'modules' => [
        'Magento_Store' => 1,
        'Magento_Directory' => 1,
        // ... all enabled modules
    ],
    'system' => [
        'default' => [
            'general' => [
                'locale' => ['code' => 'en_US'],
            ],
        ],
    ],
    'scopes' => [ /* website/store view definitions */ ],
    'themes' => [ /* active theme definitions */ ],
];
```

> **Exam focus:** `config.php` stores the **module list** AND optionally the **system configuration** (store settings). The module list is always written; the system config is only written when you explicitly dump it.

### 1.3 env.php — Structure

Created by the Magento installer or manually. Never generated by `app:config:dump`.

```php
<?php
return [
    'backend' => ['frontName' => 'admin'],
    'crypt' => ['key' => 'your-encryption-key'],
    'db' => [
        'table_prefix' => '',
        'connection' => [
            'default' => [
                'host' => 'localhost',
                'dbname' => 'magento2',
                'username' => 'magento',
                'password' => 'secret',   // SENSITIVE — never commit
                'active' => '1',
            ],
        ],
    ],
    'resource' => ['default_setup' => ['connection' => 'default']],
    'x-frame-options' => 'SAMEORIGIN',
    'MAGE_MODE' => 'developer',
    'session' => ['save' => 'files'],
    'cache' => [
        'frontend' => [
            'default' => ['backend' => 'Cm_Cache_Backend_Redis', ...],
            'page_cache' => ['backend' => 'Cm_Cache_Backend_Redis', ...],
        ],
    ],
    'lock' => ['provider' => 'db'],
    'cache_types' => [ /* cache type on/off flags */ ],
    'directories' => ['document_root_is_pub' => true],
];
```

> **Exam focus:** `env.php` is the **only** place for credentials, encryption keys, and environment-specific infrastructure config (Redis, DB). If a question asks where DB credentials live — **env.php, not config.php, not the database**.

---

## 2. The Configuration Hierarchy

This is one of the most tested architectural concepts. Three layers, each overriding the one before it.

```
Layer 1 (Lowest priority)         Layer 2                    Layer 3 (Highest priority)
+---------------------------+    +---------------------+    +---------------------------+
|  config.xml / config.php  | -> |  core_config_data   | -> |  Environment Variables    |
|  (default/module values)  |    |  (DB, Admin UI)     |    |  (env.php / shell env)    |
+---------------------------+    +---------------------+    +---------------------------+
       "What ships"                "What admin set"           "What ops team controls"
```

### 2.1 Layer 1 — Default Configuration (config.xml)

Every module declares its default config values in `etc/config.xml`:

```xml
<!-- Vendor/Module/etc/config.xml -->
<config xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
        xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="urn:magento:module:Magento_Store:etc/config.xsd">
    <default>
        <catalog>
            <frontend>
                <list_per_page>12</list_per_page>
            </frontend>
        </catalog>
    </default>
</config>
```

> **Exam focus:** `config.xml` values are the **fallback** — they apply when no Admin UI setting or env var override exists. Changing `config.xml` requires a code deployment, not just cache flush.

### 2.2 Layer 2 — Database Configuration (core_config_data)

Values saved in Admin UI → Stores → Configuration land in the `core_config_data` table.

```sql
SELECT scope, scope_id, path, value
FROM core_config_data
WHERE path = 'catalog/frontend/list_per_page';
```

| scope | scope_id | path | value |
|---|---|---|---|
| default | 0 | catalog/frontend/list_per_page | 24 |
| websites | 1 | catalog/frontend/list_per_page | 12 |

Scope hierarchy (most specific wins): `store` > `websites` > `default`

### 2.3 Layer 3 — Environment Variable Overrides

Environment variables in the format `CONFIG__<SCOPE>__<PATH_WITH_DOUBLE_UNDERSCORE>` **always win**, regardless of what the Admin UI shows.

```bash
# Format: CONFIG__<SCOPE_TYPE>__<SCOPE_CODE?>__<PATH>
# Default scope:
CONFIG__DEFAULT__CATALOG__FRONTEND__LIST_PER_PAGE=48

# Website scope (scope_id = 1, but use website code):
CONFIG__WEBSITES__BASE__CATALOG__FRONTEND__LIST_PER_PAGE=36
```

Set in `env.php` under the `system` key, or as actual OS environment variables:

```php
// env.php — env var style overrides
'system' => [
    'default' => [
        'catalog' => [
            'frontend' => [
                'list_per_page' => 48,
            ],
        ],
    ],
],
```

> **Exam focus (Critical):** After running `app:config:dump`, Admin UI fields that were dumped become **locked/greyed out**. The only ways to change them are:
> 1. Edit `config.php` directly and redeploy
> 2. Set an environment variable override
> 3. Delete the value from `config.php` (restores Admin UI editability)
>
> This is an architectural *intentional* feature — it enforces that production config is version-controlled.

### 2.4 Sensitive vs. Environment-Specific Config

| Type | Storage | Example |
|---|---|---|
| **Sensitive** | Environment variables / `env.php` ONLY | API keys, passwords, payment credentials |
| **Environment-specific** | `env.php` | DB host, Redis host, base URL |
| **System / Shared** | `config.php` (committed) | Tax classes, catalog settings, CMS blocks |

```bash
# Mark a config path as sensitive — writes to env.php, prevents it from being dumped to config.php
bin/magento config:sensitive:set payment/braintree/private_key "actual-key"
```

> **Exam focus:** Sensitive configuration paths are declared via `di.xml` by injecting into `Magento\Config\Model\Config\TypePool` — there is no `config_sensitive.xml` file type. Modules register sensitive paths by passing an array of `path => "1"` items to the `sensitive` constructor argument of `TypePool` via `di.xml`. This prevents those paths from being written to `config.php` during `app:config:dump`. A question about PCI compliance or credential handling should immediately point you toward env vars and TypePool-declared sensitive paths.

Example (from `module-paypal/etc/di.xml`):
```xml
<type name="Magento\Config\Model\Config\TypePool">
    <arguments>
        <argument name="sensitive" xsi:type="array">
            <item name="payment/payflowpro/pwd" xsi:type="string">1</item>
            <item name="payment/payflowpro/user" xsi:type="string">1</item>
            <!-- ... -->
        </argument>
    </arguments>
</type>
```

---

## 3. app:config:dump — Deep Dive

### 3.1 What It Does

```bash
bin/magento app:config:dump
```

Writes the following to `config.php`:
- **Module list** — always included
- **System configuration** — store config values from `core_config_data`
- **Scopes** — website and store view definitions
- **Themes** — active theme assignments

### 3.2 What It Does NOT Do

- Does **not** write to `env.php`
- Does **not** export sensitive config (those are filtered out by TypePool)
- Does **not** export `core_config_data` values marked as environment-specific

### 3.3 The Lock-Down Effect (Architecturally Critical)

```
Before app:config:dump:               After app:config:dump:
+------------------------+            +------------------------+
| Admin UI               |            | Admin UI               |
| [Catalog] Per Page: 24 |            | [Catalog] Per Page: 24 |
| [EDITABLE FIELD]       |            | [GREYED OUT / LOCKED]  |
+------------------------+            +------------------------+
        |                                       |
        v                                       v
  core_config_data                      config.php (authoritative)
  (authoritative)                       core_config_data (ignored for
                                        paths present in config.php)
```

**Why this exists architecturally:**
The intent is to make store configuration **reproducible across environments**. If a value is in `config.php` and committed to VCS, every environment gets identical configuration — no manual Admin UI changes that can drift between staging and production.

> **Exam focus:** The question "why is the Admin UI field locked after config:dump?" has a deeper answer than "it was dumped." The *architectural reason* is to enforce environment parity and prevent configuration drift between staging and production. This is the answer an architect is expected to give.

### 3.4 Selective Dumping

```bash
# Dump only specific config types
bin/magento app:config:dump scopes     # Only website/store scopes
bin/magento app:config:dump system     # Only system config
bin/magento app:config:dump themes     # Only theme assignments
bin/magento app:config:dump i18n       # Only translations
```

---

## 4. Environment Variables as Configuration Overrides

### 4.1 Naming Convention

```
CONFIG__<SCOPE>__<PATH_SEGMENTS_DOUBLE_UNDERSCORE>

SCOPE values:
  DEFAULT          → applies to default scope
  WEBSITES__<code> → applies to a specific website
  STORES__<code>   → applies to a specific store view
```

```bash
# Examples:
CONFIG__DEFAULT__WEB__UNSECURE__BASE_URL=https://staging.example.com
CONFIG__DEFAULT__GENERAL__LOCALE__CODE=en_US
CONFIG__WEBSITES__US__WEB__UNSECURE__BASE_URL=https://us.example.com
```

### 4.2 Adobe Commerce Cloud — Specific Env Vars

On Magento Cloud, environment variables are set via `.magento.env.yaml` or the Cloud console:

```yaml
# .magento.env.yaml (cloud-specific, NOT for app config override)
stage:
  global:
    SKIP_HTML_MINIFICATION: false
  deploy:
    CACHE_CONFIGURATION:
      _merge: true
      frontend:
        default:
          backend: Cm_Cache_Backend_Redis
```

> **Exam focus:** Cloud environment variables set in the Cloud console or `.magento.env.yaml` under the `MAGENTO_CLOUD_VARIABLES` key are different from the `CONFIG__*` pattern. Know which mechanism serves which purpose.

---

## 5. Application Modes

### 5.1 Mode Comparison Table

| Feature | `developer` | `production` | `default` |
|---|---|---|---|
| Error display | Full stack trace in browser | Suppressed (logged only) | Suppressed |
| Exception page | Detailed | Generic "We apologize" | Generic |
| Static assets | Generated on-the-fly per request | Must be pre-deployed | Generated on-the-fly |
| DI compilation | Regenerated on every request | Must be pre-compiled | Skipped |
| Symlinks for static | Yes (pub/static symlinks to source) | No (actual files copied) | No |
| Template hints | Available | Not available | Not available |
| Performance | Slow (not for prod) | Optimised | Mediocre |
| `generated/` rebuild | Automatic | Manual (`di:compile`) | Manual |

### 5.2 Switching Modes

```bash
# Check current mode
bin/magento deploy:mode:show

# Switch to developer (development environments only)
bin/magento deploy:mode:set developer

# Switch to production (triggers static content deploy + DI compile)
bin/magento deploy:mode:set production
```

### 5.3 The White Screen of Death — Mode Dependency

In **production mode**, PHP errors are suppressed. A fatal error = white screen. In **developer mode**, a fatal error shows the full stack trace.

```
Production Mode PHP Fatal Error:
+----------------------------------+
| We apologize for this inconven-  |
| ience. Please try again later.   |
+----------------------------------+
     (No stack trace visible)
     ERROR IS IN: var/log/exception.log

Developer Mode PHP Fatal Error:
+----------------------------------+
| Fatal error: Uncaught Exception  |
| Stack trace:                     |
| #0 ...Plugin.php(45): ...        |
| #1 ...                           |
+----------------------------------+
     (Full trace visible in browser)
```

> **Exam focus (Critical):** When diagnosing a white screen of death in production:
> **FIRST step = check `var/log/exception.log`**
> NOT clearing cache. NOT running di:compile. NOT switching modes.
> The exam specifically tests this ordering. Clearing cache before reading logs can destroy evidence.

## 6. Log Files — What Each Contains

### 6.1 Log File Reference Table

| File | Location | Contains | When to Check |
|---|---|---|---|
| `system.log` | `var/log/system.log` | General application notices, warnings — deprecations, non-critical errors, module info messages | Unexpected behaviour, module issues |
| `exception.log` | `var/log/exception.log` | **All uncaught exceptions** with full stack trace | White screen, 500 errors — **check FIRST** |
| `debug.log` | `var/log/debug.log` | Verbose debug output (only active in developer mode or when explicitly enabled) | Deep debugging — **disable in production** |
| `cloud.log` | `var/log/cloud.log` | Adobe Commerce Cloud platform events — hook execution, environment provisioning | Cloud deploy failures |
| `deploy.log` | `var/log/deploy.log` | Magento deploy-phase output — config import, DI compile, SCD results | Deployment failures |
| `report/` | `var/report/<id>` | Full exception reports linked from the error page (each error gets a unique ID) | When the error page shows a report number |

### 6.2 Reading exception.log

```
[YYYY-MM-DD 10:15:32] main.CRITICAL:
  Plugin class Vendor\Module\Plugin\ProductPlugin
  does not implement interface method afterGetName
  correctly — return type must be ?string, bool returned
  {"exception":"[object] (TypeError ...)"} []
```

Structure: `[timestamp] logger_name.LEVEL: message {"context"} []`

### 6.3 Enabling/Disabling debug.log

`dev/debug/debug_logging` is a **deployment config** path stored in `env.php`. It is set automatically when switching application modes, or via:

```bash
# Via setup:config:set (writes to env.php — correct command for deployment config)
bin/magento setup:config:set --enable-debug-logging=1   # Enable
bin/magento setup:config:set --enable-debug-logging=0   # Disable (MUST be 0 in production)
```

The path constant `CONFIG_PATH_DEBUG_LOGGING = 'dev/debug/debug_logging'` is defined in `Magento\Config\Model\Config\Setup\ConfigOptionsList`. Switching to production mode (`deploy:mode:set production`) automatically sets it to `0`.

> **Exam focus:** `debug.log` being enabled in production is a **security and performance risk** — it can expose sensitive data and fill disk space. The exam may present a scenario where performance degrades in production; enabling debug logging is a likely culprit.

### 6.4 Log Level Hierarchy

```
DEBUG < INFO < NOTICE < WARNING < ERROR < CRITICAL < ALERT < EMERGENCY
  |                                           |
  +--- debug.log captures these              +--- exception.log captures these
```

### 6.5 Custom Logging (Architectural Pattern)

```php
<?php
// Inject \Psr\Log\LoggerInterface — NOT \Magento\Framework\Logger\Monolog directly
// This follows PSR-3 and allows swapping the logging backend

namespace Vendor\Module\Model;

use Psr\Log\LoggerInterface;

class MyService
{
    public function __construct(
        private readonly LoggerInterface $logger
    ) {}

    public function doSomething(): void
    {
        try {
            // business logic
        } catch (\Exception $e) {
            // Log to system.log with context
            $this->logger->critical($e->getMessage(), ['exception' => $e]);
        }
    }
}
```

> **Exam focus:** Always inject `\Psr\Log\LoggerInterface`, not the concrete Monolog class. This is the architecturally correct pattern — it decouples your module from the logging implementation.

## 7. Common Failure Patterns & Diagnosis

### 7.1 White Screen of Death (WSOD)

```
Symptom: Blank page or generic error page
         No visible error

Diagnosis Flow:
  Step 1 --> check var/log/exception.log  (ALWAYS FIRST)
  Step 2 --> check var/log/system.log
  Step 3 --> check var/report/<id> if an error ID is shown
  Step 4 --> switch to developer mode (if safe) for in-browser trace
  Step 5 --> check PHP error log (/var/log/php-fpm/error.log or similar)

NOT Step 1: clearing cache (destroys evidence, may not fix root cause)
NOT Step 1: running setup:di:compile (masks the real issue)
```

**Common WSOD causes and their log signatures:**

```
exception.log signature: "Circular dependency..."
-> Cause: Circular DI — two classes inject each other (directly or transitively)
-> Fix: Inject a factory or proxy instead of the concrete class

exception.log signature: "Class ... does not exist"
-> Cause: Missing generated/ files after code changes
-> Fix: bin/magento setup:di:compile

exception.log signature: "Plugin class ... does not implement..."
-> Cause: Wrong plugin method signature / return type
-> Fix: Correct the plugin method signature

exception.log signature: "Unable to unserialize value"
-> Cause: Stale cache with old serialized data after schema/model change
-> Fix: bin/magento cache:flush
```

### 7.2 Circular Dependency (DI)

```
Class A                    Class B
+-------------+            +-------------+
| __construct |            | __construct |
| (B $b)      |<---------- | (A $a)      |
+-------------+            +-------------+
      |                           |
      +---> needs B to exist      +---> needs A to exist
            but B needs A               but A needs B
            --> DEADLOCK (Circular DI)
```

**Solution pattern — use a Proxy:**

```php
<?php
// WRONG — direct injection creating circular dependency
public function __construct(
    private readonly \Vendor\Module\Model\ServiceB $serviceB
) {}

// CORRECT — inject proxy, which defers instantiation
public function __construct(
    private readonly \Vendor\Module\Model\ServiceB\Proxy $serviceB
) {}
```

> **Exam focus:** Magento can auto-generate proxies for you, but you must declare the `\Proxy` suffix in your constructor. The architectural reason for proxies is **lazy instantiation** — the real object is only created when a method is first called, breaking the circular dependency chain.

### 7.3 Missing generated/ Directory

After pulling code changes, adding plugins, or modifying di.xml:

```bash
# Symptom: "Class Vendor\Module\Model\Something\Interceptor does not exist"
# Cause: Interceptors (plugins), factories, and proxies live in generated/

# Fix sequence:
rm -rf generated/
bin/magento setup:di:compile

# In developer mode, generated/ is rebuilt automatically per-request
# In production mode, it MUST be pre-compiled
```

> **Exam focus:** `generated/` contains **interceptors** (plugin wrappers), **factories**, **proxies**, and **extension attribute interfaces** (e.g., `generated/code/Magento/Sales/Api/Data/OrderExtensionInterface.php`). It is build-time output — it should be in `.gitignore` and regenerated as part of every deployment.

### 7.4 Stale Cache

```bash
# Specific cache types
bin/magento cache:clean config     # Clean config cache only
bin/magento cache:clean full_page  # Clean full page cache only

# All cache types — clean (removes invalid) vs flush (removes everything including non-Magento)
bin/magento cache:clean   # Preferred — only removes Magento-tagged cache
bin/magento cache:flush   # Nuclear — removes everything in cache storage
```

| Command | What it does | When to use |
|---|---|---|
| `cache:clean` | Removes only Magento-managed cache entries | After config changes |
| `cache:flush` | Empties the entire cache storage backend | When cache storage is corrupted |
| `cache:disable <type>` | Disables a cache type (performance impact) | Debugging only |

### 7.5 Cron Not Running

```bash
# Check if cron is configured (non-Cloud environments)
crontab -l | grep magento

# Expected entry:
# * * * * * php /path/to/magento cron:run 2>&1 | grep -v "Ran jobs by schedule"

# Manually trigger cron (debugging only)
bin/magento cron:run

# Run only the indexer cron group
bin/magento cron:run --group=index

# Check for stuck cron jobs
SELECT * FROM cron_schedule WHERE status = 'running' AND executed_at < NOW() - INTERVAL 1 HOUR;
```

**Note:** There is no `bin/magento cron:status` command. The available cron CLI commands are `cron:run` (with optional `--group` flag), `cron:install`, and `cron:remove`. To check cron job status, query the `cron_schedule` table directly.

**Symptoms of cron not running:**
- Indexers showing "Reindex required" indefinitely
- Newsletters not sending
- Price rules not applying
- Session cleanup not happening → disk fills up

> **Exam focus:** `cron:run --group=index` runs only indexer-group jobs (group `id="index"` in `module-indexer/etc/cron_groups.xml`). On Cloud, cron is configured in `.magento.app.yaml`, not the OS crontab.

## 8. The Correct Upgrade / Deploy Order (on-prem deployment)

This sequence is tested repeatedly. The order is not arbitrary — each step creates prerequisites for the next.

### 8.1 The Correct Sequence

```
Step 1: setup:upgrade
   |
   | Creates/updates DB schema and data.
   | Registers new modules, runs upgrade scripts.
   | MUST happen before di:compile because new classes
   | may be referenced in DI config.
   v
Step 2: setup:di:compile
   |
   | Scans all di.xml files, generates interceptors,
   | factories, proxies. Validates DI configuration.
   | MUST happen before SCD because SCD may need
   | generated classes for less/sass compilation plugins.
   v
Step 3: setup:static-content:deploy
   |
   | Copies/compiles static assets (CSS, JS, images)
   | to pub/static/. In production, assets must be
   | pre-deployed because they are NOT generated on-the-fly.
   v
Step 4: cache:flush
   |
   | Clears stale cached config, layout, block HTML.
   | Done LAST — clearing before deploy would just result
   | in cache being rebuilt with old data.
   v
   Deployment complete
```

### 8.2 Commands Reference

```bash
# Full production deployment sequence
bin/magento maintenance:enable

bin/magento setup:upgrade --keep-generated

bin/magento setup:di:compile

bin/magento setup:static-content:deploy -f \
    en_US en_GB \
    --area frontend \
    --area adminhtml

bin/magento cache:flush

bin/magento maintenance:disable
```

> **Exam focus:** The `--keep-generated` flag on `setup:upgrade` prevents deletion of the `generated/` directory, which avoids a window of downtime in production. Without it, Magento deletes `generated/` before running the upgrade, causing a brief period where interceptors don't exist.

### 8.3 Why the Order Matters (Architectural Reasoning)

| If you do X before Y | What breaks |
|---|---|
| `di:compile` before `setup:upgrade` | Compiled DI references classes from new modules that don't exist in DB yet — runtime mismatch |
| `static:deploy` before `di:compile` | LESS/SCSS compilation plugins (which are DI-based) haven't been compiled yet — CSS may fail |
| `cache:flush` before `static:deploy` | Cache is rebuilt from old static files — then flushed again on next request. Wasted work, not harmful, but architecturally sloppy |
| Skip `setup:upgrade` entirely | DB schema out of sync with code — data corruption, missing tables |

## 9. Hands-On: Breaking & Diagnosing a Plugin

### 9.1 The Setup — Create a Broken Plugin

```xml
<!-- Vendor/Sandbox/etc/di.xml -->
<?xml version="1.0"?>
<config xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
        xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="urn:magento:framework:ObjectManager/etc/config.xsd">
    <type name="Magento\Catalog\Model\Product">
        <plugin name="sandbox_product_name_plugin"
                type="Vendor\Sandbox\Plugin\ProductNamePlugin"
                sortOrder="10"
                disabled="false"/>
    </type>
</config>
```

```php
<?php
// Vendor/Sandbox/Plugin/ProductNamePlugin.php
// THIS IS INTENTIONALLY BROKEN — wrong return type

namespace Vendor\Sandbox\Plugin;

use Magento\Catalog\Model\Product;

class ProductNamePlugin
{
    /**
     * BROKEN: after-plugin for getName() must return ?string (or string)
     * We're returning bool — this will cause a TypeError at runtime
     */
    public function afterGetName(Product $subject, $result): bool  // <-- WRONG TYPE
    {
        return true;  // <-- Wrong: should return a string (the product name)
    }
}
```

### 9.2 What Happens at Runtime

1. A page loads that calls `$product->getName()`
2. Magento's ObjectManager instantiates `ProductNamePlugin\Interceptor` (generated class)
3. The interceptor calls `afterGetName()`, which returns `true` (a bool)
4. The calling code receives `true` where it expected a string
5. Depending on PHP strict types: **TypeError** thrown → **exception.log** entry → **WSOD** in production

### 9.3 Diagnosing Using Logs

```bash
# Step 1: Check exception.log FIRST
tail -n 50 var/log/exception.log
```

**Expected log output:**

```
[YYYY-MM-DD 10:23:41] main.CRITICAL:
  TypeError: Return value of Vendor\Sandbox\Plugin\ProductNamePlugin::afterGetName()
  must be of type string, bool returned
  in /var/www/html/vendor/magento/framework/Interception/Interceptor.php:135
  Stack trace:
  #0 generated/code/Magento/Catalog/Model/Product/Interceptor.php(123): ...
  #1 Magento/Catalog/Block/Product/ListProduct.php(89): ...
  {"exception":"[object] (TypeError(code: 0): ...)"} []
```

```bash
# Step 2: Trace the generated interceptor to understand the call chain
cat generated/code/Magento/Catalog/Model/Product/Interceptor.php | grep -A 20 "getName"
```

**Generated interceptor snippet (for understanding):**

```php
<?php
// generated/code/Magento/Catalog/Model/Product/Interceptor.php
// Auto-generated — DO NOT EDIT DIRECTLY

public function getName(): ?string
{
    $pluginInfo = $this->pluginList->getNext($this->subjectType, 'getName');
    if (!$pluginInfo) {
        return parent::getName();
    } else {
        return $this->___callPlugins('getName', func_get_args(), $pluginInfo);
    }
}
```

The interceptor enforces the **original method's return type** (`?string`). When your plugin returns `bool`, PHP 7.4+ strict type enforcement triggers the TypeError.

### 9.4 Diagnosing Circular DI — Log Pattern

```bash
# Intentionally create circular dependency then run:
bin/magento setup:di:compile
```

```
[Magento\Framework\Exception\RuntimeException]
Circular dependency: Vendor\Sandbox\Model\ServiceA
depends on Vendor\Sandbox\Model\ServiceB,
and Vendor\Sandbox\Model\ServiceB depends on Vendor\Sandbox\Model\ServiceA.
```

> This error appears during **compile time** (di:compile), not at runtime — which is why di:compile is so important in CI/CD pipelines. It catches these issues before deployment.

### 9.5 The Fix

```php
<?php
// Vendor/Sandbox/Plugin/ProductNamePlugin.php — FIXED

namespace Vendor\Sandbox\Plugin;

use Magento\Catalog\Model\Product;

class ProductNamePlugin
{
    /**
     * Correct after-plugin: return type must match (or be compatible with)
     * the intercepted method's return type.
     * Product::getName() returns ?string, so we must return ?string.
     */
    public function afterGetName(Product $subject, ?string $result): ?string
    {
        if ($result === null) {
            return $result;
        }
        return strtoupper($result);  // Correct: returns a string
    }
}
```

```bash
# After fixing the plugin:
rm -rf generated/
bin/magento setup:di:compile
bin/magento cache:flush
```

### 9.6 Plugin Method Signature Rules (Reference)

```php
<?php
// BEFORE plugin — runs before the method, can modify arguments
public function beforeMethodName(
    SubjectClass $subject,
    $arg1,         // original method arguments
    $arg2          // ...
): array           // Return: array of modified arguments, or null
{}

// AFTER plugin — runs after the method, receives result
public function afterMethodName(
    SubjectClass $subject,
    $result,       // return value of original method
    $arg1,         // original method arguments (PHP 7+)
    $arg2          // ...
): <return_type>   // MUST match or be compatible with original return type
{}

// AROUND plugin — wraps the method entirely
public function aroundMethodName(
    SubjectClass $subject,
    callable $proceed, // call $proceed(...$args) to invoke original
    $arg1,
    $arg2
): <return_type>
{}
```

> **Exam focus:** The most common plugin error is an **after-plugin returning the wrong type**. The return type of `afterX()` must be compatible with the intercepted method's declared return type. If the original method returns `?string`, your after-plugin must also return `?string` — returning `void`, `bool`, or `int` will cause a TypeError.

## 10. Architect-Level Decision Frameworks

### 10.1 "Where should this config live?" Decision Tree

```
Is it a secret (API key, password, token)?
  YES --> env.php / OS environment variable ONLY
  NO
    |
    Is it environment-specific (differs per environment: staging vs prod)?
      YES --> env.php or CONFIG__* env var (NOT config.php)
      NO
        |
        Should it be configurable by a merchant (non-developer)?
          YES --> Admin UI (lands in core_config_data)
                  OR config.php if it should be locked across envs
          NO --> config.xml (module default) or config.php (committed)
```

### 10.2 "Why is the Admin field locked?" — The Full Architectural Answer

The exam may present a scenario question like:

*"A merchant reports that they cannot edit the store email address in Admin UI. They have not changed any code. What is the most likely cause and what is the architecturally correct resolution?"*

**Correct answer structure:**
1. **Cause:** `app:config:dump` was run and the value was written to `config.php`. Config values in `config.php` take precedence over `core_config_data` and the Admin UI field is locked to prevent drift.
2. **Resolution options (ranked by architectural correctness):**
   - **Best:** Set an env var override (`CONFIG__DEFAULT__TRANS_EMAIL__IDENT_GENERAL__EMAIL`) — preserves config.php integrity, overrides for this environment only
   - **Acceptable:** Remove the specific key from `config.php` — restores editability but must be done on all environments
   - **Avoid:** Directly editing `core_config_data` via SQL — bypasses the config system, will be overridden by `config.php` anyway

### 10.3 Mode Selection — Architectural Criteria

| Criterion | developer | production |
|---|---|---|
| Is this a live customer-facing environment? | No | **Yes** |
| Do you need to see errors in-browser? | Yes | No |
| Will CSS/JS change frequently? | Yes (symlinked, instant) | No (deploy pipeline) |
| Is performance critical? | No | **Yes** |
| Are there CI/CD pipelines for asset compilation? | Optional | **Required** |

> **Exam focus:** Running `developer` mode in production is not just a performance issue — it is a **security vulnerability** (stack traces expose file paths, class names, and potentially sensitive data). An architect must be able to articulate both the performance *and* security reasons.

### 10.4 Log-First Debugging — The Architectural Principle

The reason exception.log must be checked **before** any remediation action:

```
Clear cache first approach (WRONG):
  Problem -> Clear cache -> May fix symptom -> Root cause unknown
                                             -> Problem recurs
                                             -> Evidence destroyed

Log-first approach (CORRECT):
  Problem -> Read exception.log -> Understand root cause -> Fix root cause
                                                         -> Verify in logs
                                                         -> Problem does not recur
```

On the exam, if a scenario offers "check logs" and "clear cache" as possible first steps — **check logs is always architecturally correct first step**.

## Quick-Reference Checklist

### Configuration Files
- [ ] `config.php` — committed to VCS, contains module list + shared system config
- [ ] `env.php` — **never** committed, contains DB, cache, crypt key, MAGE_MODE
- [ ] `config.php` is written by `app:config:dump`; `env.php` is written by the installer or manually
- [ ] After `app:config:dump`, Admin UI fields for dumped values are **locked/greyed out**
- [ ] Sensitive config (passwords, API keys) must go in `env.php` / OS env vars — **never** `config.php`

### Configuration Hierarchy (Low → High priority)
- [ ] Layer 1: `config.xml` (module defaults)
- [ ] Layer 2: `core_config_data` (Admin UI / database)
- [ ] Layer 3: Environment variables (highest priority — always wins)
- [ ] Env var format: `CONFIG__DEFAULT__SECTION__GROUP__FIELD`

### Sensitive Config Declaration
- [ ] Sensitive paths declared via `di.xml` → `Magento\Config\Model\Config\TypePool` injection (`argument name="sensitive"`, path → "1")
- [ ] **No `config_sensitive.xml` file type exists** in Magento
- [ ] `bin/magento config:sensitive:set <path> <value>` writes value to `env.php`, bypassing `config.php`

### Admin UI Lock Behaviour
- [ ] Values in `config.php` lock the corresponding Admin UI field
- [ ] To override: use `CONFIG__*` env var OR edit `config.php` directly
- [ ] To restore Admin UI editability: remove the key from `config.php`

### Application Modes
- [ ] `developer` — errors shown in browser, assets on-the-fly, DI rebuilt per-request
- [ ] `production` — errors suppressed to logs, assets must be pre-deployed, DI must be pre-compiled
- [ ] `default` — do not use in either dev or prod environments
- [ ] Running developer mode in production = security + performance risk

### Log Files
- [ ] `exception.log` — all uncaught exceptions with stack traces (**check FIRST for WSOD**)
- [ ] `system.log` — notices, warnings, non-critical application messages
- [ ] `debug.log` — verbose debug output; **must be disabled in production**
- [ ] `cloud.log` — Adobe Commerce Cloud platform/hook events
- [ ] `deploy.log` — deployment phase output (di:compile, SCD, config import)
- [ ] `var/report/<id>` — full exception reports linked from error pages

### Debug Logging
- [ ] `dev/debug/debug_logging` is a **deployment config** path stored in `env.php` — not a system config
- [ ] Disable via: `bin/magento setup:config:set --enable-debug-logging=0`
- [ ] Auto-disabled when switching to production mode (`deploy:mode:set production`)

### White Screen of Death (WSOD)
- [ ] **FIRST step: check `var/log/exception.log`** — not clearing cache
- [ ] Common causes: circular DI, missing generated/, wrong plugin return type, stale cache
- [ ] Circular DI signature in log: "Circular dependency: ClassA depends on ClassB..."
- [ ] Missing generated/ signature: "Class ...Interceptor does not exist"
- [ ] Wrong plugin type signature: "TypeError: Return value of ...afterX() must be..."

### Correct Upgrade / Deploy Order
- [ ] 1. `setup:upgrade` — sync DB schema with code
- [ ] 2. `setup:di:compile` — generate interceptors, factories, proxies
- [ ] 3. `setup:static-content:deploy` — pre-deploy assets for production
- [ ] 4. `cache:flush` — clear stale cached data
- [ ] `--keep-generated` flag on `setup:upgrade` prevents downtime window in production
- [ ] `cache:clean` = remove Magento-tagged entries; `cache:flush` = nuke entire cache storage

### Plugin Rules
- [ ] `before` plugin: return array of modified args or null
- [ ] `after` plugin: **must return type compatible with original method's return type**
- [ ] `around` plugin: must call `$proceed()` and return compatible type
- [ ] Generated interceptors live in `generated/` — never commit, always regenerate on deploy

### Circular Dependency Resolution
- [ ] Inject `\Vendor\Module\Model\ClassName\Proxy` instead of the class directly
- [ ] Proxy defers object instantiation until first method call (lazy loading)
- [ ] Circular DI is detected at **compile time** by `setup:di:compile`

### Cron
- [ ] Cron commands: `cron:run`, `cron:run --group=<group>`, `cron:install`, `cron:remove`
- [ ] **No `cron:status` command exists** — check `cron_schedule` table for job status instead
- [ ] Indexer cron group name is `index` (declared in `module-indexer/etc/cron_groups.xml`)
- [ ] On Cloud: configured in `.magento.app.yaml`, not OS crontab
- [ ] Stuck jobs in `cron_schedule` table can block subsequent runs

### Architect-Level Reasoning (Exam Differentiators)
- [ ] Config.php lock = intentional, for environment parity and drift prevention
- [ ] Log-first debugging = preserves evidence, identifies root cause vs. symptom
- [ ] `env.php` for secrets = PCI/security compliance, not just convention
- [ ] Proxy pattern for DI = lazy instantiation to break circular dependencies
- [ ] `developer` mode in production = security vulnerability (exposes internals), not just slow
- [ ] Always inject `Psr\Log\LoggerInterface`, not concrete Monolog class (PSR-3 compliance)
- [ ] `cache:clean` preferred over `cache:flush` in most cases — less destructive
